CLIFF-LEDGE layout, six dwellings occupying narrow sandstone ledges at four different heights along a forest cliff face, connected by rope-and-plank ladders spiked into the rock between levels and a single zigzag carved-stone stairway rising from the base to the topmost ledge.

HANGING-INVERTED layout, five dwellings suspended upside-down from the broad underside of a great horizontal oak limb, each hanging on braided root-cord at a slightly different drop-length, connected at their base-platforms by thin rope-span walkways strung parallel to the branch above.

LINEAR-PROCESSIONAL layout, seven dwellings strung in a winding single-file line along a narrow deer-track path threading through old-growth pine forest, each placed roughly twelve paces from the next, the path connecting every threshold in an unbroken meandering chain from first to last.

AMPHITHEATER-TIERED layout, eight dwellings arranged across four curved hillside terraces, two dwellings per terrace stepping down toward a flat central clearing, connected by short timber-ramp staircases at each terrace edge and lateral stone-slab paths running the length of each tier.

ROOTBALL-NEST layout, four dwellings tucked into the hollow pockets and arching gaps of an enormous upturned rootball from a fallen ancient oak, connected by short rope-ladder spans strung between the exposed roots and a single worn dirt path circling the rootball's outer base.

MUSHROOM-RING layout, six dwellings encircling a tight ring of waist-high giant shelf-mushrooms at even intervals, connected by a continuous ring-path of flat white pebbles looping around the mushroom cluster, with short spoke-paths leading outward into the surrounding forest from alternating dwellings.

WATERFALL-LEDGE layout, five dwellings arranged on three mossy rock ledges beside a two-tier forest waterfall, two dwellings on the broad lower ledge flanking the plunge pool, two on the narrow mid ledge, one at the crest, connected by carved-stone steps and rope-rail ladders at each drop.

ISLAND-GROVE layout, three dwellings clustered on a small circular island in the center of a still forest pond, reached from the bank by a chain of eleven flat stepping-stones curving in a gentle arc, the dwellings arranged in a tight triangle around a single central elder-tree.

CRESCENT-MOON-ARC layout, seven dwellings arranged in a smooth crescent arc around the open face of a small woodland meadow, their thresholds all oriented inward toward the meadow center, connected by a continuous curved gravel path tracing the inner edge of the arc from horn to horn.

TERRACED-HILLSIDE layout, six dwellings stepped down a moss-covered slope across three terraces of two dwellings each, each terrace cut level into the hillside, connected by broad log-slab staircases dropping between tiers and lateral packed-earth paths running the width of each terrace.

BOULDER-CLUSTER layout, five dwellings nestled into the crevices and sheltered faces of a tight granite boulder cluster, each dwelling wedged against its own boulder surface, connected by a winding stone-flag path threading through the gaps and over one low saddle-bridge of flat stones spanning two boulders.

SPIRAL-ASCENT layout, four dwellings positioned at quarter-turn intervals along a great spiraling exposed root that corkscrews up from the forest floor to a height of thirty feet, each dwelling on its own flat root-section, connected by the continuous spiraling surface of the root itself and short rope-rail spans at steeper sections.

TWIN-CANOPY layout, seven dwellings split between two adjacent ancient chestnuts — four in the first canopy and three in the second — each tree's dwellings linked internally by short rope-span bridges, with one long central suspension bridge of woven vine and split-timber planks connecting the two canopies at their closest point.

CROSSROADS layout, five dwellings clustered around a four-way intersection of wide forest paths, one dwelling anchoring each of the four path-corners and one set at the exact crossing-center on a raised circular earth mound, connected by the four radiating paths and a ring-path looping the central mound.

SINGLE-SOLITARY layout, one dwelling perched at the crown of a moss-covered boulder at the center of a rain-cleared meadow, open sky above, knee-high grass pressing in on all sides, no path leading to it, only a ring of bare earth at the boulder's base.

CLUSTER layout, seven dwellings scattered across a shallow forest hollow, winding bark-chip paths threading between each, the lowest three nestled near the hollow's floor and the upper four climbing its gentle slope, no two dwellings facing the same direction.

CANOPY-NETWORK layout, eight dwellings distributed among five ancient beeches, linked by a continuous web of braided-vine bridges and knotted-rope spans, bark-plank walkways circling each trunk, the whole network forming a loose oval sixty feet above the leaf litter.

VERTICAL-STACK layout, five dwellings mounted at ascending heights on a single massive cedar trunk, each resting on its own cantilevered root-wood platform, spiral bark-carved stairs winding the trunk between them, the topmost dwelling level with the first high branches.

OVER-WATER layout, four dwellings positioned along a slow forest brook, two on each bank, connected by a flat stepping-stone ford at the narrowest crossing and a woven-branch arch-bridge twenty paces upstream, water audible beneath both crossings.

FAIRY-RING-COURTYARD layout, nine dwellings set in a precise circle around a wide courtyard of pale compacted sand, eight narrow stepping-stone spokes radiating from a flat central hearthstone to each dwelling's threshold, every gap between dwellings equal.

CLIFF-LEDGE layout, six dwellings occupying natural stone ledges at five different heights on a mossy cliff face, connected by rope-and-plank ladders pinned to the rock and a zigzagging series of carved-stone footholds, the topmost ledge nearly at the cliff's overhang.

HANGING-INVERTED layout, five dwellings suspended upside-down beneath three enormous horizontal oak limbs, each hanging from a separate braided-root cord, swaying gently, accessed by knotted-rope ladders descending from the branch above, spacing irregular but roughly alternating.

LINEAR-PROCESSIONAL layout, six dwellings spaced at even intervals along a gently curving forest track, smooth river-pebble paths connecting threshold to threshold, the track bending just enough that each dwelling sees only its two nearest neighbors, the ends of the line invisible from the middle.

AMPHITHEATER-TIERED layout, eight dwellings arranged on four concentric stone-and-turf tiers descending toward a flat circular stage of bare earth, two dwellings per tier, connected by short turf-cut ramps on the left flank and carved-root steps on the right.

ROOTBALL-NEST layout, four dwellings tucked into the cathedral of upturned roots of a long-fallen ancient oak, each occupying a separate root-framed alcove, connected by a network of packed-dirt lanes running between the root columns, the whole village sheltered inside the root mass.

MUSHROOM-RING layout, six dwellings encircling an uneven ring of giant wild mushrooms, each dwelling backed against a mushroom's stalk, connected by a looping gravel path that passes each threshold in sequence, the inner ring of mushroom caps forming a canopy over the central open space.

WATERFALL-LEDGE layout, five dwellings on three tiered rock ledges beside a narrow forest waterfall, two on the lowest spray-wet ledge, two on the mid-ledge, and one at the top beside the pour-point, connected by carved-stone switchback stairs and one rope-railed bridge spanning the falls midway.

ISLAND-GROVE layout, three dwellings clustered in the center of a small moss island in a still forest pond, reached from the bank by a line of eleven unevenly spaced stepping-stones, the island's shore edged with exposed roots, no bridge, the water shallow but dark.

CRESCENT-MOON-ARC layout, seven dwellings arranged in a wide crescent around a still pool, their open faces all oriented toward the water, connected by a continuous curved flagstone path tracing the inner arc, the two horn-ends of the crescent left open to the surrounding forest.

TERRACED-HILLSIDE layout, six dwellings stepped down a fern-covered hillside across four terraces cut into the slope, the upper terrace holding one dwelling and each lower terrace holding two, connected by narrow stone-slab stairs descending the center and earthen ramps on either side.

TWIN-CANOPY layout, seven dwellings split across two neighboring canopy giants — four in the left crown, three in the right — each tree's dwellings linked internally by vine-rope bridges, the two canopies joined by a single long rope-plank suspension span at the midpoint of both crowns.

STORK-NEST layout, four dwellings each mounted atop its own tall straight post driven into a broad boggy clearing, platforms at unequal heights between eight and fifteen feet, connected only by rope-ladder spans strung post to post in a rough square, the bog floor undisturbed below.

HONEYCOMB-CELL layout, six dwellings fitted into a grid of hexagonal alcoves carved into a soft sandstone bank, arranged in two rows of three, each cell separated from its neighbors by a thin stone wall, connected by a continuous flat stone ledge running the full width of both rows.

SPIRAL-ASCENT layout, five dwellings positioned at intervals along a massive corkscrew root that winds forty feet upward around the base of an ancient yew, each dwelling anchored to a flat section of the root's outer curve, connected by the root itself serving as a continuous spiral walkway, the spacing widening toward the top.

SINGLE-SOLITARY layout, one dwelling perched at the crest of a mossy limestone outcrop surrounded by open meadow, no paths leading to it, only a worn trail of flattened grass circling the base of the rock, the nearest treeline a distant dark border.

CLUSTER layout, six dwellings arranged in a loose irregular scatter across a sun-warmed forest floor clearing, narrow dirt-and-pebble paths threading between each, the gaps filled with low creeping moss, no two dwellings equidistant, the grouping weighted slightly toward the eastern edge.

CANOPY-NETWORK layout, eight dwellings distributed across five interlocked ancient beeches, joined by a continuous web of vine-rope bridges, knotted-cord ladders descending each trunk, and narrow plank-walkways lashed to the largest limbs, the whole network forming an unbroken aerial loop.

OVER-WATER layout, five dwellings positioned along both banks of a wide slow-moving forest brook, three on the northern bank and two on the south, connected by two flat stone-slab bridges and a third upstream crossing of steppingstone rounds spaced a half-pace apart.

AMPHITHEATER-TIERED layout, seven dwellings arranged across three concentric stepped hillside terraces curving around a flat circular stage of packed earth at the base, connected by short flights of stone steps cut into the slope and narrow lateral paths running the length of each tier.

VERTICAL-STACK layout, five dwellings ascending a single massive ancient chestnut trunk at staggered heights, each resting on its own cantilevered bark-plank platform, linked by a continuous spiral staircase of wooden pegs driven into the bark and short rope-ladder spans between each level.

FAIRY-RING-COURTYARD layout, nine dwellings arranged in a precise circle around a wide central courtyard of tamped bare earth, eight dwellings evenly spaced around the ring and one set at the exact center, with spoke-pattern stepping-stone paths connecting the central dwelling to each of the eight outer ones.

CLIFF-LEDGE layout, six dwellings distributed across four natural sandstone ledges at varying heights on a mossy cliff face, the lower three ledges connected by iron-peg ladders driven into the stone and rope handrails, the highest ledge reached only by a long knotted-rope rappel line.

TERRACED-HILLSIDE layout, four dwellings descending a steep moss-covered hillside on four distinct flat-cut terraces, each terrace wider than the one above, connected by zigzagging stone-and-root staircases and a central straight stepped path running directly down the fall-line of the slope.

SUSPENDED-BASKET layout, five dwellings hanging in woven-withe pendant baskets from a single enormous horizontal oak branch, spaced at unequal intervals along its length, each basket reachable by a thin rope-ladder descending from the branch above and a swinging bridge linking adjacent baskets laterally.

CRESCENT-MOON-ARC layout, seven dwellings arranged in a broad open crescent arc facing a still central forest pool, the two end dwellings closer to the water's edge and the central dwelling set farthest back, connected by a curved gravel path running the full arc and two short radial paths to the pool.

LINEAR-PROCESSIONAL layout, eight dwellings strung in a gently winding single-file line along a narrow moss-edged forest trail, each separated from the next by a gap of roughly equal length, the trail itself serving as the sole connective path, stone markers placed at each gap-midpoint.

ROOTBALL-NEST layout, six dwellings tucked into the cavernous upturned root mass of a fallen ancient oak, three nestled in deep root-framed alcoves and three resting atop the exposed upper root ridges, connected by a network of short rope-bridges spanning the root gaps and plank ramps climbing the ridges.

TWIN-CANOPY layout, seven dwellings split between two adjacent canopy giants — four in the crown of a silver birch and three in a neighboring hornbeam — linked by one long main rope-span bridge at midheight and two secondary vine-rope bridges higher and lower, with knotted-cord ladders on each trunk.

BOULDER-CLUSTER layout, five dwellings nestled into the sheltered gaps between and atop a cluster of four granite boulders, two on the ground between the stones and three on upper boulder surfaces, connected by rope-loop ladders scaling the boulder faces and a narrow path looping the cluster's base.

MUSHROOM-RING layout, six dwellings arranged in a loose ring around a close cluster of giant mushrooms at the center, each dwelling facing inward toward the ring, connected by a circular beaten-earth path linking all six and short spoke-paths cutting inward to the mushroom cluster's base.

HONEYCOMB-CELL layout, six dwellings fitted into six hexagonal alcoves carved into a soft earthen bank, arranged in two staggered rows of three, each alcove opening onto a shared timber-plank walkway running the full width of the bank face, with a ladder at each end descending to ground level.

ISLAND-GROVE layout, four dwellings occupying a small densely wooded island in the center of a quiet forest pond, reachable by two routes — a line of eleven flat stepping stones from the eastern bank and a narrow plank-bridge from the western — with a looping dirt path connecting all four dwellings on the island.

SPIRAL-ASCENT layout, four dwellings positioned at quarter-turn intervals along a single enormous corkscrew root that spirals upward from the forest floor to the height of the surrounding canopy, each dwelling on a flattened platform cut into the root's outer curve, connected by the root's own spiraling surface path and short rope-ladder drops between levels.

STORK-NEST layout, five dwellings each elevated on a separate tall post-and-platform structure rising from the forest floor at varying heights between knee-height and twice the height of a standing adult, the platforms connected by a web of rope-span bridges at multiple levels and individual rope-ladder descents to the ground beneath each post.

SINGLE-SOLITARY layout, one dwelling perched alone atop a wide flat granite outcropping at the forest edge, the stone surface bare and wind-scoured around it, no path leading in, the nearest treeline a full clearing-width away on every side.

CLUSTER layout, seven dwellings grouped in a loose scatter across a mossy hollow between the roots of three ancient beeches, narrow dirt paths threading between each, a small fire-pit clearing at the center where all paths loosely converge, no dwelling touching another.

CANOPY-NETWORK layout, eight dwellings distributed across five tall oaks, linked by a continuous web of vine-rope bridges and knotted-cord ladders, plank walkways circling individual trunks at each node, the whole network suspended twenty feet above the forest floor in one unbroken web.

VERTICAL-STACK layout, five dwellings ascending a single massive chestnut trunk at measured intervals, each mounted on its own bracketed platform, connected by a continuous spiral of wooden-rung ladder winding the bark face, the lowest dwelling just above root height and the highest lost in lower canopy.

OVER-WATER layout, four dwellings arranged around a wide forest pool, two on the mossy north bank, one on a flat midstream stone, and one on the far south bank, connected by a sequence of stepping-stone crossings and one arched plank-bridge at the narrow western neck.

FAIRY-RING-COURTYARD layout, nine dwellings placed in a precise circle around a central courtyard of smooth bare earth, stepping-stone paths radiating from the courtyard center to each dwelling threshold like spokes of a wheel, the ring uniformly spaced with identical gaps between each structure.

CLIFF-LEDGE layout, six dwellings occupying natural ledges on a sandstone cliff face at four different heights, connected by a zigzag of rope-and-plank ladders pinned to the rock between levels and a narrow switchback path climbing the cliff base to the lowest ledge.

HANGING-INVERTED layout, five dwellings suspended upside-down from a broad horizontal oak limb by heavy braided-vine hangers, each hanging at a slightly different length so their bases form a staggered descending line, short rope-ladder spans linking each pendant structure to the next.

LINEAR-PROCESSIONAL layout, six dwellings spaced at regular intervals along both sides of a gently curving forest path, three on each side facing inward, connected by the shared packed-earth path with a flat stepping-stone threshold marking each dwelling's entry point.

AMPHITHEATER-TIERED layout, eight dwellings arranged on four grass-cut terraces stepping up a south-facing hillside, two dwellings per tier, connected by short stone-slab stair-flights between each level, all dwellings oriented to face a flat open stage-area at the hill's base.

ROOTBALL-NEST layout, four dwellings tucked into the cavernous upturned root-mass of a fallen ancient oak, each nestled within a separate root-framed alcove, connected by short rope-ladder climbs between upper and lower root cavities and a single packed-earth path skirting the root base.

MUSHROOM-RING layout, six dwellings arranged in a ring encircling a naturally occurring cluster of giant bracket fungi, each dwelling set between two fungal growths, connected by a continuous circular path of flat stones with equal spacing between each dwelling and its neighbors.

WATERFALL-LEDGE layout, five dwellings on three spray-dampened ledges cut into the mossy rockface beside a narrow forest waterfall, two dwellings on the widest middle ledge, connected by rope-and-timber ladders mounted to the wet stone between levels and a plank walkway spanning the falls-face at mid-height.

ISLAND-GROVE layout, four dwellings clustered on a small tree-covered island in the center of a quiet forest pond, reached from both banks by two separate chains of wide stepping-stones, the dwellings arranged in a loose square around a central island clearing with no internal paths.

CRESCENT-MOON-ARC layout, seven dwellings forming a curved crescent arc along the eastern rim of a circular moss-meadow, the open mouth of the crescent facing west toward the meadow's center, connected by a continuous curved gravel path running the inner face of the arc with equal spacing between each dwelling.

TERRACED-HILLSIDE layout, six dwellings stepped down a north-facing hillside on five moss-edged terraces, one dwelling per terrace except the widest middle terrace which holds two, connected by stone-slab stair-flights between each level and a single vertical rope-ladder as a shortcut at the steepest section.
